candidate.statement: Breast cancer cell lines with ERBB2 amplification have stronger dependency on ERBB2 knockout than non-amplified lines.
queries: ERBB2 amplification ERBB2 dependency breast cancer CRISPR
HER2 amplified breast cancer ERBB2 essentiality DepMap
ERBB2 knockout breast cancer dependency screen

review.rationale: The candidate hypothesis proposes that breast cancer cell lines with ERBB2 amplification have stronger dependency (more negative dependency score, direction -1) on ERBB2 knockout than non-amplified lines. MED:41090369 analyzed Cancer Dependency Map (DepMap) CRISPR knockout and shRNA knockdown datasets alongside ERBB2 genomic alterations and targeted inhibitor sensitivity. It demonstrates that ERBB2-amplified breast cancer cell lines are specifically sensitive to ERBB2 CRISPR knockout and shRNA knockdown compared to non-amplified lines (e.g., EGFR-mutant lines showed no significant reduction in viability upon ERBB2 knockout or knockdown). Furthermore, MED:41609417 specifically identifies ERBB2 as a top expression-driven and genomic dependency in cancer cell lines. Thus, primary empirical DepMap screen evidence directly supports the hypothesis in both population and direction.

candidate.statement: Breast cancer cell lines with RB1 loss exhibit reduced dependency on CDK4 knockout compared to RB1-intact breast cancer lines.
queries: RB1 loss CDK4 dependency breast cancer CRISPR
RB1 status CDK4 essentiality breast cancer cell lines
RB1 deficiency CDK4 dependency breast DepMap

review.rationale: In functional dependency screens (such as Cancer Dependency Map CRISPR data) and cell cycle biology studies, loss/deficiency of the retinoblastoma protein (RB1) renders cancer cells intrinsically independent of CDK4/6 activity. Specifically, MED:35235778 directly demonstrates using CRISPR screens across cancer lines that RB-deficient models are intrinsically CDK4/6-independent, whereas RB-proficient models exhibit CDK4 dependency. Furthermore, MED:41595248 explicitly documents from DepMap analysis and functional genomics that loss of RB function via RB1 mutations/deletions marks cell-intrinsic independence from CDK4 and CDK6, whereas intact RB status (especially in breast adenocarcinomas) is strongly associated with CDK4 dependency. Thus, breast cancer cell lines with RB1 loss have reduced dependency on CDK4 knockout compared to RB1-intact breast cancer lines (direction = 1, indicating positive difference/higher dependency score meaning less essential).

queries: RB1 loss CDK6 dependency breast cancer CRISPR
RB1 loss CDK6 essentiality breast cell lines DepMap
RB1 mutant CDK6 knockout dependency breast cancer

review.rationale: The candidate hypothesis posits that breast cancer cell lines with RB1 loss show reduced dependency on CDK6 knockout compared to RB1-wildtype breast cancer lines (direction = 1 in DepMap CERES/Chronos, meaning higher dependency score / less essential). Multiple sources in the provided text substantiate this: MED:41595248 explicitly states that functional genomics across DepMap show loss of RB function marks cell-intrinsic independence from CDK4 and CDK6, with RB loss being a canonical marker of CDK4/6 independence. In addition, MED:41390513 analyzes DepMap CRISPR knockouts and specifically lists the RB1-CDK6 interaction as an established resistance interaction where RB1 loss-of-function/mutation confers resistance to CDK6 loss (positive genetic effect score). Furthermore, MED:35235778 notes that RB-deficient models are intrinsically CDK4/6 independent.

candidate.statement: Breast cancer cell lines with PTEN loss exhibit increased dependency on PIK3CB (p110beta) knockout compared to PTEN-intact lines.
queries: PTEN loss PIK3CB dependency breast cancer CRISPR
PTEN loss p110beta essentiality breast cell lines
PIK3CB dependency PTEN mutant breast cancer DepMap

review.rationale: MED:41708282 directly demonstrates in a human mammary epithelial cell transformation model that knocking out PTEN drives dependence on the p110β subunit of PI3K (encoded by PIK3CB). Furthermore, MED:37120674 identifies PTEN and PIK3CB as a strong synthetic lethal interaction using cell line and cancer multi-omics data. While MED:34417459 notes complexity in prostate cancer, the evidence specifically in mammary models directly supports that PTEN loss induces dependency on PIK3CB (p110β).
